'''William Howard Casey''' (born 1955) is [[distinguished professor]] of chemistry and professor of geology at the [[University of California, Davis]]. He has made major contributions in the fields of aqueous geochemistry and inorganic solution chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1016/j.gca.2017.01.018| title=Citation for presentation of the 2016 C.C. Patterson Award to William H. Casey| journal=Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta| volume=201| pages=430–431| year=2017| last1=Swaddle| first1=T.| bibcode=2017GeCoA.201..430S}}</ref> He has in particular received international awards for his work on the use of heteronuclear ambient and high-pressure [[Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy|NMR spectroscopic]] and [[Mass spectrometry|mass spectrometric]] techniques in elucidating the solution chemistry of discrete metal oxide clusters such as aluminum hydroxides and polyoxoniobates, and has been elected Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] and Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].
The mineral Caseyite<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mindat.org/min-53574.html | title=Caseyite: Mineral information, data and localities}}</ref> is named in his honour.

==Education==
Casey obtained a B.A. from [[University of the Pacific (United States)]] in 1976,<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://chemistry.ucdavis.edu/people/william-casey |title = William Casey|date = 2016-10-27}}</ref> an M.Sc. from the [[University of California, Davis]] in 1980 and a Ph.D. from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1985.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.eag.eu.com/awards/science-innovation-award/about-william-casey/ | title=About William Casey « European Association of Geochemistry}}</ref> Following five years as a geochemist at [[Sandia National Laboratories]] he was appointed professor in Geology at [[University of California, Davis]] in 1991, and professor in Chemistry in 2005.

==Awards==
* [[Fellow of the American Chemical Society|Fellow, American Chemical Society]], 2019
* [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|Fellow, American Association for the Advancement of Science]], 2017
* [[Clair Patterson#Memorials|Clair C. Patterson Award]], Geochemical Society, 2016
* [[Science Innovation Award]] The Science innovation award and Werner Stumm medal, 2010
* Fellow, [[Geochemical Society]]
* Fellow, [[European Association of Geochemistry]]
